summary: Milestone 1 Accounts & Foundations verified end-to-end. Backend: 23/24 pytest tests passed, 1 skipped (reset-password flow) because the Emergent email proxy returned 429 → backend leaked 502 instead of the generic 202 (same bug observed on /auth/register). All auth state transitions behave correctly: register→verify issues tokens, login 401/403/429 lockout, refresh rotation (old token invalidated), logout, reset-password revokes sessions, change-password revokes sessions & reissues tokens, GET/PATCH /api/me validations (rate >500 rejected, invalid category rejected, hourly_rate round/clear), DELETE /api/me (wrong pw 400, correct removes user and blocks subsequent login). Frontend (390x844 mobile viewport): welcome → sign-in → home works; set-rate banner present before rate, hidden after; Profile edit saves £30.00/hr and Account row reflects it; Messages card opens Messages screen; Security row navigates to Security screen (Face ID switch, change password form, delete account row visible); Sign-out returns to welcome without a confirm dialog; tab navigation across Home/Shifts/Earnings/Account works. Deprecated packages detected: none (expo-av/expo-barcode-scanner/expo-background-fetch not used).

critical.issue: Returns 502 'Failed to send email' when the Emergent email proxy is rate-limited (429 'rate_limited'). Should swallow the delivery failure and always return the generic 202 — otherwise it (a) leaks email-send telemetry (enumeration signal: distinguishes 'email tried & failed' from the normal 202), and (b) is user-visible: the Register screen displays 'Something went wrong. Please try again.' even though the user is persisted in Mongo and a code is in db.action_codes. See server.py register(); email_service.send_email() currently only maps insufficient_credits/integration_disabled/daily_limit_reached to a soft response — add 'rate_limited' (and generally swallow for 202-generic endpoints).

Same root cause as register: Emergent proxy 429 → backend 502 instead of generic 202. Causes the pytest TestResetPassword to skip when rate-limited. Fix in email_service._post / send_email error-mapping or wrap the call in forgot_password/register/resend-verification with try/except so the generic 202 is always returned (log the delivery failure).

minor.issue: RegisterIn.full_name is not stripped before uniqueness/duplicate checks. Not blocking; strip happens at insert.

integration_issues.issue: When backend returns 502 due to email proxy rate-limit (see backend_issues), the Register screen shows 'Something went wrong. Please try again.' and the user cannot proceed to the verify screen even though the account was created. Backend fix will resolve this.

issues: First paint sometimes shows an empty hero before DutyConnect branding + bullets appear (observed as a near-blank screen in one capture). After full load the welcome screen renders correctly.

react_native_issues.issue: Console warning: '"shadow*" style props are deprecated. Use "boxShadow".' Replace shadow* RN style props with boxShadow (RN Web) or platform-split styles.
Console warning: 'props.pointerEvents is deprecated. Use style.pointerEvents' — move pointerEvents to the style object on affected components.

action_items: Backend: in email_service.send_email treat 'rate_limited' like insufficient_credits/daily_limit_reached (soft-fail), and for generic 202 endpoints (/auth/register, /auth/resend-verification, /auth/forgot-password) always return 202 even on email failure (log the error). This fixes both the enumeration signal and the user-facing register error.
Frontend: migrate deprecated RN-Web style props: shadow* → boxShadow and props.pointerEvents → style.pointerEvents.
Confirm welcome screen hero/branding renders on first paint (hydration flash).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: register() and forgot_password() place send_email outside a try/except — any 502/503 bubbles up and breaks the generic-202 contract.

server.py register duplicate branch: if existing unverified user has an in-flight verify code (recently_sent) the response is 202 but no new code is sent — this is correct, just verify UI messaging matches.
email_service.send_email: error-code allowlist is hardcoded; prefer always-swallow for 202-generic callers via a parameter (e.g., swallow=True).
No file exceeds 700 lines; Mongo ObjectId correctly excluded via projection; env vars used throughout.

success_rate.backend: 95.8% (23/24 passed, 1 skipped due to email proxy rate-limit)

seed_data_creation: Tests create ephemeral delivered+t1_<tag>@resend.dev accounts and delete them in teardown. Main user delivered+t1@resend.dev password restored to Testpass123, hourly_rate reset to None, login_attempts cleared.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Run pytest with `-n 0` (serial) because class/method tests share the single main user and the login-lockout test will race with concurrent main_user_tokens fixtures otherwise. Email proxy on this environment is heavily rate-limited (~1 req/sec sustained → 429); space email-sending calls or expect transient 502s from register/forgot-password until the backend soft-fail fix lands. Dev codes are in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log — grep '[DEV] <kind> code for user <uid>:'. If main user gets locked out: db.login_attempts.delete_many({}) in test_database.
rca_of_issue: Both failing/skipped tests have the same RCA: the Emergent-managed email proxy (POST /api/v1/email/send) returns 429 {code: 'rate_limited'} when called in bursts (observed throughput ~1 req/s). email_service.send_email maps 429/'rate_limited' to a generic HTTPException(502). register(), resend-verification() and forgot_password() invoke send_email without catching, so the 502 propagates. For the 202-generic contract this (1) leaks whether the system attempted a send, (2) surfaces to the frontend as a hard error on the Register screen even though the user has been persisted. Mitigation: catch delivery errors inside the three generic endpoints and still return the GENERIC_SENT payload with status 202; log the delivery failure for ops. Reproduction: run pytest serially twice in a minute, or in UI flow register two accounts <1s apart.
